description: handleCreate: `nick, _, err := nicknameField(fields)` followed by an `if err != nil` 400 return was replaced with `nick, _, _ := nicknameField(fields)`, discarding the nickname decode error.
trigger: POST /users with a valid name and email and a non string, non null nickname, e.g. {"name":"a","email":"a@x","nickname":42}.
symptom: Creating a user with a malformed nickname succeeds with 201 and the user has no nickname, instead of the request being rejected with 400.

class: nil dereference or nil map write
description: Store.Update: nickname branch `} else if p.Nickname != nil {` changed to `} else if p.Nickname != nil && *p.Nickname != *u.Nickname {` (skip unchanged nickname), which dereferences u.Nickname even when the stored user has no nickname.
trigger: Create a user without a nickname, then PATCH /users/{id} with {"nickname":"bob"}.
symptom: Setting a nickname on a user who never had one fails: the server drops the connection with no response (a handler panic is logged), and the nickname is never set.

class: missing case in a switch over a closed set
description: handlePatch: the `case errors.Is(err, errDuplicateEmail): writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, ...)` arm was removed from the switch over Store.Update's error outcomes, so the duplicate email error falls into `case err != nil` (500).
trigger: Create two users, then PATCH the second with {"email": <first user's email>}.
symptom: Changing a user's email to one that already belongs to another user returns 500 internal error instead of 409 conflict.

description: Store.Delete takes `s.mu.RLock()` / `defer s.mu.RUnlock()` instead of `s.mu.Lock()` / `defer s.mu.Unlock()`, so it mutates the users and byEmail maps while holding only a shared read lock.
trigger: Concurrent DELETE requests (or DELETE concurrent with GET /users or GET /users/{id}) for different users.
symptom: Under concurrent deletes the whole server process crashes intermittently with 'fatal error: concurrent map writes' (or map read and write), or the race detector flags store access.

description: readFields now reads the body in a goroutine that sends on an unbuffered channel, and the caller selects between that channel and r.Context().Done(). When the context wins, the caller returns and the reader goroutine blocks forever on `done <- readResult{...}`.
trigger: POST or PATCH where the client disconnects (or the request context is canceled) before the body has been fully read, e.g. send headers with Content-Length and a partial body, then close the connection.
symptom: Goroutine count and memory grow steadily over time when clients abort uploads; goroutine dumps show many goroutines stuck in a channel send under readFields.

class: lost update (copy modified, never written back)
description: Store.Update: the final `s.users[id] = u` write back was removed; the local copy u is modified and returned but the map keeps the old value (the byEmail index is still updated).
trigger: PATCH /users/{id} with any change (e.g. {"name":"new"}), then GET /users/{id}.
symptom: PATCH responds 200 with the new values, but subsequent GETs and the list still show the old values; after an email change, the old email is free and the new email is reported as taken while the user still shows the old one.

description: validateName: `n > 100` changed to `n >= 100`, so the upper bound is exclusive.
trigger: POST /users or PATCH with a name of exactly 100 characters.
symptom: A name of exactly 100 characters is rejected with 400 'name must be 1 to 100 characters'.

class: wrong HTTP status or error kind
description: handleCreate: success response `writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, u)` changed to `writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, u)`.
symptom: Creating a user returns 200 OK instead of 201 Created.

class: wrong time, backoff, or limit arithmetic
trigger: POST or PATCH with a JSON body larger than 1024 bytes, e.g. a nickname of 2000 characters (nickname has no length limit).
symptom: Requests with moderately sized bodies (over about 1 KB) fail with 400 'could not read body' even though they are well under the intended 1 MB limit.

description: Store.Update: `if p.Email != nil && *p.Email != u.Email {` changed to `if p.Email != nil && *p.Email == u.Email {`.
trigger: PATCH /users/{id} with {"email": a new unused address}, or with the user's current email.
symptom: Changing a user's email to a new address returns 200 but the email is unchanged; re-sending the user's current email returns 409 conflict.
